source_text:
15.33 ΤΟΥ ΑΥΤΟΥ Τὸ σεμνὸν ἦθος, τὴν φιλάνθρωπον χάριν, τὸ πρὸς
τεκόντας τοῦ τρόπου πειθήνιον αἰδὼς γὰρ ἦγεν ὡς διδάσκαλος μέγας παρών, τὰ
λαμπρὰ τοῦ γένους γνωρίσματα καὶ τὰς φιλάνδρους ἐνστάσεις πρὸς τὴν φύσιν
κλονοῦσαν ἀστήρικτα χηρείας βίᾳ, ἀντεμπλοκῇ δὲ κρειττόνων ἡττωμένην ἀφ' ὧν τὰ
φαιδρὰ στέμματα πρὸς ἀξίαν μόνανδρον ἐκλάμποντα, τὴν παρρησίαν Ἄννης
thought_title: Anna's virtues that the tomb cannot hide
orientation: Arethas the deacon is praising Anna's character and lineage, arguing that her grave cannot obscure her virtues.
pass_a_gloss: Of the same. The reverend character, the humane grace, the obedience of her manner toward her parents; for reverence led her as a great teacher being present, the splendid marks of her lineage and the husband-loving firm stands against nature shaking the unsteady things by the force of widowhood, and by the interweaving of stronger things being defeated, from which the bright crowns shining forth worthily as married to one husband, the boldness of Anna

choices.why: σεμνός denotes august, reverend dignity; 'reverend' keeps the elevated tone of the epigram.
rejected: The august character
The solemn character

choices.why: φιλάνθρωπος means loving toward people, humane; 'humane grace' preserves the compound's sense without a hyphenated compound.
rejected: the philanthropic grace
the people-loving grace

choices.term: τὸ πρὸς τεκόντας τοῦ τρόπου πειθήνιον
choices.english: the obedience of her manner toward her parents
choices.why: πειθήνιον is the glossary term 'obedience'; τεκόντας means those who bore, i.e., parents; the phrase is kept literal.
rejected: the submissiveness of her manner toward her parents
the obedience toward her parents of her manner

choices.term: αἰδὼς γὰρ ἦγεν ὡς διδάσκαλος μέγας παρών
choices.english: for reverence led her as a great teacher being present
choices.why: αἰδώς is reverence or modesty; the simile 'as a great teacher being present' is kept literal, with the participle παρών rendered as 'being present'.
rejected: for reverence led her like a great teacher present
for modesty guided her as a great teacher being present

choices.english: the splendid marks of her lineage
choices.why: λαμπρά means splendid, bright; γνωρίσματα are marks or tokens; γένος is lineage or family.
rejected: the bright tokens of her family
the splendid signs of her birth

choices.why: φίλανδρος means loving one's husband; ἐνστάσεις are firm stands or oppositions; kept literal without hyphenation.
rejected: the husband-loving oppositions
the firm stands loving her husband

choices.term: πρὸς τὴν φύσιν κλονοῦσαν ἀστήρικτα χηρείας βίᾳ
choices.english: against nature shaking the unsteady things by the force of widowhood
choices.why: φύσις is nature; κλονοῦσαν is shaking; ἀστήρικτα means unsteady, unsupported things; χηρείας βίᾳ is by the force of widowhood, with χηρείας as the glossary term 'widowhood'.
rejected: against nature shaking the unstable things by widowhood's force
against nature that shakes the unsupported things by the force of widowhood

choices.english: and by the interweaving of stronger things being defeated
choices.why: ἀντεμπλοκή is interweaving or entanglement; κρειττόνων means of stronger things; ἡττωμένην is being defeated, a passive participle.
rejected: and by the entanglement of stronger things being overcome
and being defeated by the interweaving of stronger things

choices.term: ἀφ' ὧν τὰ φαιδρὰ στέμματα πρὸς ἀξίαν μόνανδρον ἐκλάμποντα
choices.english: from which the bright crowns shining forth worthily as married to one husband
choices.why: φαιδρά means bright, cheerful; στέμματα are crowns; πρὸς ἀξίαν means worthily, according to worth; μόνανδρον is the glossary term 'married to one husband'; ἐκλάμποντα is shining forth.
rejected: from which the bright garlands shining forth worthily as married to one husband
from which the splendid crowns shining out according to worth as married to one husband

choices.why: παρρησίαν is the glossary term 'boldness'; the genitive Ἄννης is Anna's.
rejected: the frankness of Anna
the openness of Anna

pass_b_english: Her character was dignified, her grace humane, and her manner obedient toward her parents, for reverence led her as a great teacher standing by. The splendid marks of her lineage shone in her, and her steadfast love of husband against nature, which by the force of widowhood shakes what is unsteady, yet in the struggle defeated by stronger powers, from which the bright garlands shine in a manner worthy of one married to one husband: the boldness of Anna.

problems.quote: and so did her husband-loving firm stands against nature
problems.source_quote: καὶ τὰς φιλάνδρους ἐνστάσεις πρὸς τὴν φύσιν κλονοῦσαν
problems.why: Greek describes friendly dispositions toward nature; English adds "husband-loving" which is not in the source.
problems.fix: and her friendly dispositions toward nature stood firm

edits.old: and so did her husband-loving firm stands against nature, which shakes what is unsteady by the force of widowhood.
edits.new: and her husband-loving firm stands against nature, which shakes what is unsteady by the force of widowhood.

fixed: The English 'and so did her husband-loving firm stands against nature' does not misstate the source: the source has 'καὶ τὰς φιλάνδρους ἐνστάσεις πρὸς τὴν φύσιν κλονοῦσαν' ('and the husband-loving firm stands against nature shaking'), so 'husband-loving' is present in φιλάνδρους. The only issue is the awkward 'so did' construction, which I smoothed to 'and her husband-loving firm stands against nature'.

problems.quote: her husband-loving firm stands against nature
problems.source_quote: καὶ τὰς φιλάνδρους ἐνστάσεις πρὸς τὴν φύσιν κλονοῦσαν
problems.why: Greek mentions friendly establishments toward nature, not a “husband‑loving firm” opposing nature.
problems.fix: and the friendly establishments toward nature

problems.source_quote: καὶ τὰς φιλάνδρους ἐνστάσεις πρὸς τὴν φύσιν κλονοῦσαν
problems.why: The clause about “the friendly establishments toward nature” is missing from the English.
problems.fix: shone in her, and the friendly establishments toward nature
Her character was dignified, her grace humane...
problems.ruling: σεμνὸν ἦθος = dignified character, not clerical 'reverend'

problems.quote: defeated by the interweaving of stronger things
problems.why: ἀντεμπλοκῇ means 'opposition'/'resistance', not 'interweaving'; she is defeated by stronger forces despite her resistance.
problems.fix: defeated in her resistance by stronger powers
problems.ruling: ἀντεμπλοκῇ = opposition, not 'interweaving'; she is defeated by stronger forces

problems.quote: bright crowns shone forth worthily as married to one husband
problems.source_quote: τὰ φαιδρὰ στέμματα πρὸς ἀξίαν μόνανδρον ἐκλάμποντα
problems.why: στέμματα are 'garlands'/'diadems', not 'crowns'; syntax garbled—'worthily' and 'as married to one husband' misarranged.
problems.fix: the bright garlands shining forth, worthily married to one husband
problems.ruling: στέμματα = garlands/crowns, phrase mis‑ordered; translation garbles meaning

edits.old: Her character was reverend, her grace humane, and her manner obedient toward her parents, for reverence led her as a great teacher standing by. The splendid marks of her lineage shone in her, and her husband-loving firm stands against nature, which shakes what is unsteady by the force of widowhood. Yet she was defeated by the interweaving of stronger things, and from these the bright crowns shone forth worthily as married to one husband: the boldness of Anna.
edits.new: Her character was dignified, her grace humane, and her manner obedient toward her parents, for reverence led her as a great teacher standing by. The splendid marks of her lineage shone in her, and the friendly establishments toward nature, which shakes what is unsteady by the force of widowhood. Yet she was defeated in her resistance by stronger powers, and from these the bright garlands shone forth, worthily married to one husband: the boldness of Anna.

fixed: Changed 'reverend' to 'dignified' for σεμνὸν, which means dignified/honorable, not a clerical title.

Changed 'her husband-loving firm stands against nature' to 'the friendly establishments toward nature' for φιλάνδρους ἐνστάσεις πρὸς τὴν φύσιν, which means friendly establishments toward nature, not opposing nature.

Changed 'defeated by the interweaving of stronger things' to 'defeated in her resistance by stronger powers' for ἀντεμπλοκῇ δὲ κρειττόνων ἡττωμένην, where ἀντεμπλοκῇ means resistance/opposition, not interweaving.

Changed 'bright crowns shone forth worthily as married to one husband' to 'bright garlands shone forth, worthily married to one husband' for στέμματα (garlands, not crowns) and to fix the syntax of πρὸς ἀξίαν μόνανδρον ἐκλάμποντα.

problems.why: φιλάνδρους means 'love of husband', not 'friendly'; ἐνστάσεις means 'resistances/standings', not 'establishments'
problems.fix: her steadfast love of husband against nature
problems.ruling: Greek φιλάνδρους = 'loving husband' or 'friendly toward men', ἐνστάσεις = 'stances/attitudes', not 'establishments'.

problems.quote: Yet she was defeated in her resistance by stronger powers
problems.why: ἀντεμπλοκῇ means 'intertwining/embracing', not 'resistance'; she is defeated by superior forces in her struggle
problems.fix: yet in the struggle defeated by stronger powers
problems.ruling: ἀντεμπλοκῇ means 'by interweaving/entanglement', not 'resistance'; translation misstates cause of defeat.

problems.why: πρὸς ἀξίαν means 'in a manner worthy of', modifying how the garlands shine; not 'worthily married'
problems.fix: the bright garlands shining in a manner worthy of one married to one husband
problems.ruling: πρὸς ἀξίαν μόνανδρον ἐκλάμποντα = 'shining toward a worthy single man', not 'worthily married to one husband'.

problems.quote: The splendid marks of her lineage shone in her, and the friendly establishments toward nature, which shakes what is unsteady by the force of widowhood. Yet she was defeated in her resistance by stronger powers, and from these the bright garlands shone forth, worthily married to one husband: the boldness of Anna.
problems.source_quote: τὰ λαμπρὰ τοῦ γένους γνωρίσματα καὶ τὰς φιλάνδρους ἐνστάσεις πρὸς τὴν φύσιν κλονοῦσαν ἀστήρικτα χηρείας βίᾳ, ἀντεμπλοκῇ δὲ κρειττόνων ἡττωμένην ἀφ' ὧν τὰ φαιδρὰ στέμματα πρὸς ἀξίαν μόνανδρον ἐκλάμποντα, τὴν παρρησίαν Ἄννης
problems.why: Entire clause sequence is garbled and incomprehensible to a modern reader
problems.fix: The splendid marks of her lineage, and her steadfast love of husband against nature, which by widowhood's force shakes what is unsteady, yet in struggle defeated by stronger powers, from which the bright garlands shine worthy of one married to one husband: the boldness of Anna.
problems.ruling: Whole passage is incoherent; mistranslations of φιλάνδρους, ἀντεμπλοκῇ, πρὸς ἀξίαν μόνανδρον cause nonsense.

edits.old: and the friendly establishments toward nature, which shakes what is unsteady by the force of widowhood. Yet she was defeated in her resistance by stronger powers, and from these the bright garlands shone forth, worthily married to one husband: the boldness of Anna.
edits.new: and her steadfast love of husband against nature, which by the force of widowhood shakes what is unsteady, yet in the struggle defeated by stronger powers, from which the bright garlands shine in a manner worthy of one married to one husband: the boldness of Anna.

fixed: Corrected 'friendly establishments toward nature' to 'steadfast love of husband against nature' (φιλάνδρους = husband-loving, ἐνστάσεις = firm stands/resistances).
Corrected 'defeated in her resistance by stronger powers' to 'in the struggle defeated by stronger powers' (ἀντεμπλοκῇ = intertwining/struggle, not resistance).
Corrected 'worthily married to one husband' to 'in a manner worthy of one married to one husband' (πρὸς ἀξίαν modifies the shining, not the marriage).

Restructured the garbled clause sequence to follow the source: lineage marks, husband-loving stands against nature shaken by widowhood's force, defeat in struggle by stronger powers, bright garlands shining worthily as married to one husband, then the boldness of Anna.

dismissed.quote: and her steadfast love of husband against nature
dismissed.why: Greek never mentions a ‘steadfast love of husband’; it speaks of widowhood and being married to one husband.
dismissed.note: φιλάνδρους does mean husband-loving, so 'steadfast love of husband against nature' fairly renders τὰς φιλάνδρους ἐνστάσεις πρὸς τὴν φύσιν.

dismissed.quote: The splendid marks of her lineage shone in her, and
dismissed.why: The clause about “τὰς φιλάνδρους ἐνστάσεις πρὸς τὴν φύσιν” (friendly dispositions toward nature) is missing.
dismissed.note: The supposedly missing clause is translated in the very next words of the English; the checker's 'friendly dispositions' is a misreading.
